project.name: Pulse — Productivity Tracking (developer guide)
project.description: Design and specification package for "Pulse", a Productivity Tracking proof-of-concept for warehouse operations, containing a PostgreSQL 15+ database schema (targeting Azure Database for PostgreSQL) and a build-task spreadsheet. It also includes static HTML wireframes for the worker mobile screens (W1-W16) and the supervisor web screens (S1-S9).

nodes.name: Productivity Tracking - Database Schema.sql
nodes.summary: PostgreSQL 15+ DDL for the Pulse productivity-tracking POC (Azure Database for PostgreSQL, schema pt, IST time zone). It defines 23 UUID-keyed, site-scoped tables covering people, setup, ASNs, activities, receiving, stock, movements, quality and review, plus an audit trigger, 16 indexes, 8 reporting views, and commented retention and row-level-security recipes.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses PostgreSQL features to enforce business rules in the database: STORED generated columns for PO-number normalisation, partial (unique) indexes such as one running activity per worker, num_nonnulls() CHECKs for exclusive polymorphic references, sequences for human-readable codes, FILTER aggregates and window functions in views, and a PL/pgSQL audit trigger.

nodes.name: Productivity Tracking - Build Tasks.xlsx
nodes.summary: Sprint and PR build-task tracker for the Pulse POC: 9 sprints (Foundations to Hardening) and 38 PRs in dependency order. Each PR row lists its branch, area, scope, wireframe screens, database tables, done-when criteria and status (all merged). Further sheets cover Git conventions and an extra-work log of fixes, reviews and test runs.

nodes.name: site
nodes.summary: Root tenant table for warehouses (sites): UUID site_id PK, unique site_code (e.g. BOM-3), name and is_active flag. Every business table carries a site_id foreign key to it.

nodes.name: employee
nodes.summary: Workers and supervisors keyed by a unique numeric employee_code, with role CHECK (worker/supervisor), home_site_id FK, password_hash, must_change_password, status (active/locked/inactive) plus failed_login_count and a locked_at consistency CHECK, and a self-referencing created_by.

nodes.name: location
nodes.summary: Scannable warehouse places per site, typed shelf, packing_area or dock, with the label location_code unique per site (UNIQUE site_id, location_code), name, is_active and created_by employee.

nodes.name: activity_type
nodes.summary: Fixed lookup of the six activities (unload, check, put_away, pick, pack, load) with display name, sort_order and the destination_type a move must end on; seeded by an INSERT in the script.

nodes.name: activity_setting
nodes.summary: Per-site, per-activity target_minutes and auto_close_minutes (composite PK site_id + activity_type) with CHECK auto_close_minutes > target_minutes; a BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger records every change in setting_change.

nodes.name: setting_change
nodes.summary: Append-only change history for activity settings: field (target_minutes or auto_close_minutes), old and new value, changed_by and changed_at. Filled by trg_activity_setting_history.

nodes.name: asn_upload
nodes.summary: Records each ASN file upload with file_name, accepted/rejected status, row_count, row-level errors in jsonb and uploaded_by; a CHECK requires errors when the upload is rejected.

nodes.name: asn
nodes.summary: Advance Shipping Notices from suppliers: asn_number unique per site, po_number with a STORED generated po_number_norm (upper case, spaces and PO prefix stripped) for matching, supplier, expected_date and a status lifecycle (expected, partly_received, received, closed) tied to closed_at by CHECK. Partial index asn_match_idx covers open ASNs by normalised PO.

nodes.name: asn_line
nodes.summary: Expected product lines of an ASN: line_no (unique per ASN), product_code, description, expected_qty > 0 and unit (boxes/pallets/pieces/other); asn_line_product_idx indexes upper(product_code) for case-insensitive line pairing.

nodes.name: activity
nodes.summary: One unit of work (unload, check, put away, pick, pack or load) per site, with a human activity_code (e.g. PA-5095) unique per site, started_by and status (running/completed/auto_closed) tied to ended_at by CHECK. Target and auto-close minutes are copied in at start so setting changes are never backdated; indexed by site and start time.

nodes.name: participant
nodes.summary: One row per worker on an activity (shared activities have several): joined_at/stopped_at, stop_type (manual/auto_closed), rework_seconds excluded from work time, and supervisor correction fields for auto-closed stops. UNIQUE (activity_id, employee_id) and the partial unique index participant_one_running allow only one open activity per worker.

nodes.name: event_log
nodes.summary: Raw log of every tap and scan: identity bigint PK, event_type, jsonb payload, device_time vs server_time and optional employee/activity links. Indexed by site + server_time and by activity; purged after 6 months.

nodes.name: receipt
nodes.summary: One row per unloaded delivery, linked to its Unload activity, with invoice header fields (number, date, PO, supplier), a generated po_number_norm and the raw Azure Document Intelligence result in ai_raw jsonb. The ASN link and asn_status (matched/chosen_from_list/no_asn) are kept consistent by CHECK.

nodes.name: receipt_line
nodes.summary: Per-product line of a receipt comparing expected (ASN), invoice and counted quantities. It stores the AI-read value with a low-confidence flag, an optional asn_line link, result_vs_asn and result_vs_invoice outcome codes and counted_by; UNIQUE (receipt_id, line_no) and an index on asn_line_id.

nodes.name: lot
nodes.summary: A received product batch created from exactly one receipt line (unique receipt_line_id), with an auto-generated lot_code (LOT-1001 sequence), description, optional AI-suggested name for deliveries without an invoice, unit and received_qty > 0.

nodes.name: pack
nodes.summary: Packed shipping unit with an auto-generated pack_code (PACK-301 sequence), the Pack activity that created it, an optional dock location and status open/at_dock/loaded. CHECKs require a location at the dock and loaded_at once loaded; load_activity_id links the Load activity.

nodes.name: portion
nodes.summary: A piece of a Lot sitting in one place. Part-moves split a portion (parent_portion_id self-reference), so live portions always add up to the Lot's received_qty. Holds qty, status (in_stock/in_pack/loaded) with location/pack CHECKs and an is_defective flag; indexed on location (in-stock only), lot and pack.

nodes.name: movement
nodes.summary: Never-edited stock-movement ledger: movement_type (unload_place, check_move, put_away, pick, pack_add, pack_to_dock, load, correction), activity, performer, lot/portion/source_portion/pack, qty, from/to locations (must differ) and is_flagged_wrong. Indexed by activity, lot + time and destination + time.

nodes.name: check_result
nodes.summary: Outcome of a Check activity on a portion: qty, pass/fail result, reason_codes text[] and description (a fail requires one of them), a stayed_on_location flag and checked_by.

nodes.name: defect_mark
nodes.summary: Defective flag placed on a portion by a failed check and later cleared by a supervisor with a note. cleared_by and cleared_at must be set together, and the partial unique index defect_mark_open allows at most one open mark per portion.

nodes.name: wrong_movement
nodes.summary: Report of a misplaced move found via shelf_scan or invoice_rescan: the flagged movement (kept), the original employee, the reporter, the activity in which it was found, reasons or a description (one required), the correction movement and rework start/end times.

nodes.name: photo
nodes.summary: Links to photos held in blob storage (invoice_page, product, defect, wrong_movement) with page_no and exactly one owner among receipt, check_result or wrong_movement (num_nonnulls CHECK). Kept for 1 year.

nodes.name: review_item
nodes.summary: Supervisor review-queue entries of five types (auto_closed, receipt_difference, asn_closed_incomplete, wrong_movement, defective). Each points to exactly one subject row, enforced by num_nonnulls and per-type CHECKs, and carries open/resolved status, decision, note and resolver; partial index on open items by site and type.

nodes.name: v_participant_time
nodes.summary: Each worker's working minutes on an activity: joins participant to activity, takes the corrected or actual stop (or now) minus rework_seconds, and carries the target snapshot.

nodes.name: v_activity_quantity
nodes.summary: Quantity handled per activity, summing movement qty for normal move types and leaving out correction moves (rework).

nodes.name: v_activity_time
nodes.summary: Total job minutes per activity, from the first worker joining to the last stopping, with a participant count. Rework time is subtracted only when one person did the job.

nodes.name: v_participant_share
nodes.summary: Each worker's time-based share of a job, built on the three base views with window functions: share_fraction, share_qty, credited target and job minutes, and job_productivity_pct (target / job minutes x 100).

nodes.name: v_worker_day
nodes.summary: Per worker, per IST day totals behind the dashboard's "By worker" view: activity count, worked minutes, items credited and a share-weighted productivity_pct.

nodes.name: v_stock_on_location
nodes.summary: Current in-stock quantity per location and lot (location_code, lot_code, description, unit and a has_defective flag), totalling portions joined to lot and location.

nodes.name: v_lot_balance
nodes.summary: Control check that compares each Lot's received_qty with the sum of its portions and exposes a balanced boolean, guarding the portion-split invariant.

nodes.name: v_asn_line_received
nodes.summary: Quantity received so far against each ASN line: sums counted_qty from receipt lines across deliveries next to expected_qty.

nodes.name: trg_activity_setting_history
nodes.summary: PL/pgSQL BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger function on activity_setting that writes target_minutes and auto_close_minutes changes (old value, new value, changed_by) into setting_change, and stamps updated_at on update.

nodes.name: Productivity Tracking - Build Plan.pdf
nodes.summary: Build Plan v1.2 (20 Oct 2026) for the Pulse productivity-tracking POC. It fixes the tech stack (Python 3.12 FastAPI with SQLAlchemy 2/Alembic on Azure Database for PostgreSQL B2s; one React + TypeScript + Vite PWA whose role decides between worker W1-W16 and supervisor S1-S9 screens; Azure Blob Storage, Document Intelligence, AI Vision, Key Vault and Application Insights). It also sets out the architecture (REST plus WebSocket live updates, APScheduler jobs for auto-close, retention and invoice reading, business rules in backend services) and the repository layout. The work is split into 38 single-feature PRs across Sprints 0-8 (Foundations, Identity and setup, Activity engine, Scanning and stock, Unload, Move activities, Quality and review, Supervisor insight, Hardening), with a dependency chain, phase milestones, development conventions (one branch per feature, Alembic migrations, site scoping, +05:30 times), risks, inputs needed from Kuehne + Nagel, and about USD 80-85 a month in Azure running costs.
nodes.languageNotes: 16-page PDF; the text was extracted with pdftotext. Its sprint tables map each PR-NN to the wireframe screens it delivers and to its 'done when' criteria. The full task list lives in Productivity Tracking - Build Tasks.xlsx.

nodes.name: Productivity Tracking - Data Model.pdf
nodes.summary: Data Model v1.2 (17 Oct 2026) documents the PostgreSQL 15+ schema (pt schema) that Productivity Tracking - Database Schema.sql creates. It covers 23 tables in eight groups (sites and people, setup, ASNs, receiving, stock, work, quality, supervisor review) with field types, rules and allowed values. It also explains how each workflow writes data: start/join/stop, auto-close, Unload with count, Put away/Pick full and part-moves, Check, Pack/Load, wrong movement, ASN upload/close, settings and login lockout. Key decisions: UUID keys with separate human codes (LOT-/PACK-/PA-), site_id on almost every table for multiple warehouses, IST timestamptz, whole-number quantities, and no deletes (only photos after 1 year and the event log after 6 months are purged). Targets and expected quantities are copied onto records when they are created, a trigger records settings history, and 8 views calculate worked minutes, job productivity, time-based shares, stock on a location and Lot balance.
nodes.languageNotes: 26-page PDF; the field tables lost their column alignment in text extraction, so treat the SQL script as the source of truth for exact column/type pairs. The document states that the script was tested on PostgreSQL 17.

nodes.name: Productivity Tracking - Developer Feature Guide.pdf
nodes.summary: Developer Feature Guide v1.7 (17 Oct 2026, prepared for Kuehne + Nagel) is the plain-language functional specification of the Pulse POC. It describes one web app with one Employee-ID login (lock after 5 wrong tries), where the role decides between phone worker screens W1-W16 and desktop supervisor screens S1-S9; supervisors on a phone get the worker screens. It covers the six warehouse activities (Unload, Check, Put away, Pick, Pack, Load) and the core ideas: location barcodes with destination-type checks, Lots and portions, packed units, Defective marks, and activity records where every tap is timestamped. It also specifies shared activities with QR join and a time-based quantity split, one running activity at a time, auto-close, wrong-movement rework time, PO-based ASN matching (Match/Short/Extra/Missing/Not on ASN/Unit differs), supervisor setup with change history and non-backdated targets, the review queue, stock and traceability, five dashboard views with Excel export, changes from the original POC document, and open assumptions.
nodes.languageNotes: 17-page PDF. Sections 3-4 (key ideas and shared features) are the prerequisites that every activity section in 5-6 builds on; section 11 lists assumptions still to be confirmed with K+N, such as PO numbers on invoices and counting at the dock.

nodes.name: Six warehouse activities
nodes.summary: A product moves through six activities: Unload, Check, Put away, Pick, Pack and Load. Each activity type has a required destination location type: a shelf for Unload, Check and Put away; a packing area for Pick; a dock for Pack.

nodes.name: Activity and participant records
nodes.summary: An activity is one job (for example one Put away), and each worker on it is a participant with their own join and stop times. A worker can have only one running participation at a time (enforced by a unique index), and every tap and scan is also timestamped in the event log.

nodes.name: Shared activity and time-based productivity
nodes.summary: Several workers can do one job together. The starter shares a QR code with a short activity code (e.g. PA-5095), and co-workers join with their join time as their start time. Quantity is shared by worked time (share = total x my time / everyone's time), and job productivity (target / job time from first join to last stop) is credited to everyone in proportion to their share.

nodes.name: Target times, auto-close and setting snapshots
nodes.summary: Supervisors set a target time and an auto-close limit for each activity type and site; the limit must be longer than the target, and every change is logged in a history table. Activities copy both values when they start, so target changes are never backdated. A background job auto-closes forgotten participations and sends them to the review queue.

nodes.name: Locations and barcodes
nodes.summary: Every shelf, packing area and dock has a printed barcode label showing its code, name and type, and workers can type the code if a label will not scan. Supervisors can create a range of shelves in one go, and moves are checked against the destination type and refused if they return to the source.

nodes.name: Lot and portion stock model
nodes.summary: A Lot (LOT-1001) is one invoice, one product and the quantity counted at Unload; it is never created from an ASN. As stock moves it is split into portions, which always add up to the Lot's received quantity. Portions show what is where now, and the never-edited movement ledger shows how it got there.

nodes.name: Packed unit
nodes.summary: At Pack, portions from one or more Lots are combined into a packed unit with an auto-generated Pack ID (PACK-301) that the worker writes on the package by hand. The unit then moves as one item, keeps a full contents list, and goes from open to at_dock to loaded.

nodes.name: Invoice reading and Unload count
nodes.summary: At Unload, multi-page invoice photos are read by Azure Document Intelligence; fields the AI is unsure about are highlighted and can be edited, and if there is no invoice, AI Vision suggests a product name. For each line the worker sees Expected, Invoice and Counted quantities and must tick every line before confirming. Each counted line becomes one Lot placed with a shelf scan.

nodes.name: ASN upload and matching
nodes.summary: Supervisors upload Advance Shipping Notices from a template, and invalid files are rejected with errors listed by row. At Unload the receipt is matched to an open ASN by normalised PO number (no spaces, upper case, no PO- prefix), with fallbacks to choosing from a list or 'No ASN'. Each line gets results vs ASN and vs invoice (match/short/extra/missing/not_on_asn/unit_differs), and ASN status moves from expected to partly_received, received or closed.

nodes.name: Check result and Defective mark
nodes.summary: At Check a worker marks a quantity Pass or Fail; a Fail needs a reason and puts a Defective mark on that portion only. Anyone who scans the location afterwards sees a non-blocking warning, and only a supervisor can clear the mark, which is never deleted.

nodes.name: Wrong movement and rework
nodes.summary: During Put away or Pick a worker can report an earlier wrong move, found by shelf scan or invoice re-scan. The original movement is flagged (never deleted), a correction movement is recorded, and the rework time is kept apart from normal productivity while the activity timer is paused.

nodes.name: Supervisor review queue
nodes.summary: One supervisor queue collects auto-closed activities, receipt/ASN differences, ASNs closed incomplete, wrong movements and defective products. Workers are never blocked; supervisors resolve each item with a decision (e.g. end_time_corrected, reviewed, mark_cleared), an optional note, and who and when.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Hub page ("Pulse, screen by screen") for the worker-app wireframes. It groups all 16 worker screens W1-W16 into Getting started, Working together, Scanning, Unload, Check/Pack/Load and Quality and finish, each card giving the screen code, name and purpose. Feature cards link to the live Showcase and to the Supervisor portal (desktop screens S1-S9), and a shared Night shift/Daylight switcher saves the chosen theme for every screen.
nodes.languageNotes: Mostly inline CSS. The screen cards are generated from a nested JS array (group, colour, [code, slug, name, description, icon]) whose code-slug pairs build the hrefs. Every Pulse page contains the same theme-and-fit IIFE, which stores the theme under the localStorage key "pulse-theme" and adds the "All screens" link back to this page.

nodes.name: Pulse-showcase.html
nodes.summary: Showcase page for the Pulse concept ("Every move counted. Effortlessly." - warehouse productivity for Kuehne + Nagel). It shows the W2 Home and W3 Running activity phones side by side as one connected prototype. Visitors can tap an activity tile to start the timer, tap the big step button to simulate a scan, and slide to stop. The completion overlay then shows their time and share, and the Home "My day" rings and activity and item counters go up.

nodes.name: W1-login.html
nodes.summary: Worker login screen (W1), the first screen when the app opens. The worker enters a numeric Employee ID and a password (with Show/Hide and "Remember my Employee ID") to start a shift. Login stays disabled until both fields are filled, errors never say which field was wrong, the account locks after 5 wrong passwords, and "Forgot your password?" sends the worker to their supervisor. A successful login goes to W2 Home, or to W3 if an activity is still running. A state previewer shows the empty, remembered, filled, wrong-password, offline and locked states.
nodes.languageNotes: The background is a warehouse aisle drawn in SVG with a vanishing-point projection and a seeded random generator, so the layout is the same on every load. An embedded base64 photo replaces it when present.

nodes.name: W2-home.html
nodes.summary: Worker home screen (W2), shown after login. It has a greeting with the date and Employee ID, "My day" rings (time working, activities done, items moved, filling toward the worker's own usual day rather than a company target), a live pill for the running activity, a "Join a co-worker" QR entry, and six colour-coded activity tiles (Unload, Check, Put away, Pick, Pack, Load) with today's counts. Only one activity can run at a time. A confirm sheet saves the start time on Start and opens W3, or W8 Invoice photo for Unload. Join opens W5, the avatar logs out to W1, and a one-off notice appears after an activity was auto-closed.

nodes.name: W3-running.html
nodes.summary: Running activity screen (W3), one screen used by all six activities. It shows a progress ring in the activity colour around a live timer, who is working (alone or with co-workers), and the activity's steps marked done, current or next, with one big button for the next scan or action. Examples: Unload (invoice read, ASN matched, place products on shelves), Put away and Pick (source and destination scans), Pack and Load (add items). Share opens W4, Wrong move opens W15 (Put away and Pick only), and step buttons lead to W6, W7, W8, W12, W13 or W14. Slide-to-stop goes to W16 and asks first if a worker alone has unfinished steps. Going back to W2 keeps the timer running.

nodes.name: W4-share.html
nodes.summary: Share activity screen (W4), opened from Share on W3. It shows a large black-on-white QR code and a short activity code (e.g. PA-5095) so co-workers can join the running activity by tapping "Join a co-worker" on their own phone (W5, then W3). "Working on this" lists everyone on the activity with their own live time, counted from when they joined. The code stops working once everyone has stopped. Done returns to W3, and a button simulates co-workers joining.

nodes.name: paintRun
nodes.summary: Redraws both showcase phones for the current activity: accent colours, icons, step list, ring progress (done steps / total), "Step n of m" captions, the main button label and the live pill. The Wrong move chip appears only for Put away and Pick.

nodes.name: scan
nodes.summary: Simulates the barcode scan for the current step: shows a spinner, then after 900 ms marks the step scanned, redraws and shows the result (e.g. "Shelf B1").

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Ends the simulated activity after slide-to-stop. It shows the completion overlay with the elapsed time and the worker's quantity share (or a not-recorded message if steps were not scanned), moves the "My day" rings forward, and raises the activities and items-moved counters.

nodes.name: login
nodes.summary: Simulates sending the login form: shows a spinner and disables the button, then after 900 ms either switches to the wrong-credentials state (when the password is "wrong") or shows that the worker is going to W2 Home.

nodes.name: setState
nodes.summary: Switches the login mock-up between preview states (empty, remembered ID, filled, wrong ID or password, no connection, account locked). It sets the error or warning banner, prefills the fields, shakes the form on errors and hides the Log in button when the account is locked.

nodes.name: openSheet
nodes.summary: Opens the Start confirmation sheet for the tapped activity tile. Start leads to W8 Invoice photo for Unload and to W3 Running activity for every other activity.

nodes.name: setState
nodes.summary: Switches Home between the idle, activity-in-progress and last-activity-auto-closed previews. It shows the live pill or the auto-close notice and locks the tiles and Join button while an activity runs.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Draws the running-activity screen from the activity's settings: ring colour and progress, "Started hh:mm, Step n of m", who is working (solo or with Employee 117), the step list, the main and Finish-pack buttons, and the Share and Wrong move chips. Each button shows where it would go (W4, W14, W15).

nodes.name: scan
nodes.summary: Handles the main step button. For Pack and Load it points to the item list and scan screens (W13, W6). For other activities it simulates the scan, marks the current step saved with its result and makes the next step current.

nodes.name: stopNow
nodes.summary: Handles slide-to-stop. A worker alone with unfinished steps gets a "Stop now?" sheet warning that anything not scanned will not be recorded; otherwise the activity stops and goes to W16 Activity complete.

nodes.name: drawQR
nodes.summary: Draws a fake 33x33 QR code in SVG, with the three corner finder patterns, timing lines and seeded random cells, from the numeric part of the activity code, always black on white.

nodes.name: people
nodes.summary: Builds the "Working on this" list: you plus any co-workers who joined, each with their join time and own live timer, a JUST JOINED tag and slide-in animation for the newest, or a waiting spinner when nobody has scanned yet. It also updates the participant count.

nodes.name: W5-join.html
nodes.summary: Worker mobile wireframe (W5 Join activity), opened from 'Join a co-worker' on W2 Home. A camera scanner reads the QR code on a co-worker's Share screen, then a confirm sheet shows the activity type, who started it and when, how many people are working, the current step and the activity code. Tapping Join starts the worker's own time and opens the shared W3 Running activity. Error sheets cover being busy in another activity (one activity at a time), an activity that has ended, and a barcode that is not an activity code. Cancel returns to W2.
nodes.languageNotes: Self-contained static prototype: about half the file is inline Pulse CSS. Inline JS simulates scan outcomes through a 'Preview a state' panel, and toast messages stand in for real navigation.

nodes.name: setState
nodes.summary: Drives the W5 prototype state machine. It shows the confirm sheet when an activity code is found, or one of three error sheets (busy in another activity, activity ended, not an activity code), and wires the error buttons to go to the worker's own W3 activity or back to W2 Home.

nodes.name: W6-fetch.html
nodes.summary: Worker mobile wireframe (W6 Scan location) for fetching product from a source shelf, packing area or dock during Check, Put away, Pick, Pack and Load. After scanning or typing the location code, the worker sees the location card and the product (selected automatically, or chosen from a dropdown when there are several). It also shows a Defective warning if the product failed Check, the Lot, invoice, supplier and on-location quantity, and a quantity stepper that splits what moves from what stays (a partial move creates a portion of the Lot). Confirm leads to W7 Scan destination, W12 Pass/Fail for Check, or W13 Item list for Pack/Load. An empty location offers W15 Report wrong movement, and Cancel returns to W3.
nodes.languageNotes: Per-activity mock data (the DATA object keyed by activity) feeds a template-string render function, so one HTML file previews five activity variants and seven scan outcomes.

nodes.name: setState
nodes.summary: Switches between the camera, the type-code sheet and the scan-result states (one product, several products, defective, empty, unknown). For result states it resets the selected product, pre-fills the quantity with the full amount on the location, and re-renders.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Builds the scanned-location result view. It shows the location card with a product count and either an automatically selected single product or a dropdown when there are several. It adds a Defective banner from a failed Check, Lot/invoice/supplier/quantity details, and either a quantity stepper or a 'packed units move as one' note. It also renders the empty-location and unknown-barcode error panels.

nodes.name: updQty
nodes.summary: Validates the quantity being moved (at least 1, no more than what is on the location) and shows the moving vs staying split for partial moves. It then wires Confirm to continue to W7 Scan destination, W12 Pass/Fail (Check) or W13 Item list (Pack).

nodes.name: W7-destination.html
nodes.summary: Worker mobile wireframe (W7 Scan destination) that records where a product or packed unit was placed. The camera title names the expected location type (shelf for Unload, Check and Put away; packing area for Pick; dock for Pack), and a pill shows what is moving. A success view shows From and To, the item, lot and quantity, plus what stayed behind after a part move. Error sheets reject a wrong location type, the source location itself, and unknown barcodes. Confirm move saves the movement and returns to W3 with the step ticked; for Unload it moves on to the next product line.

nodes.name: setAct
nodes.summary: Loads destination data for the selected activity (expected location type, From and To, item, lot, quantity, part-move remainder) into the camera pill and the success view. It wires Confirm move to save and return to W3, or for Unload to continue to the next product line.

nodes.name: setState
nodes.summary: Toggles the camera, type-code and success views. It shows a validation error sheet when the scanned location is the wrong type for the activity, is the same as the source, or is not a known barcode.

nodes.name: W8-invoice-photo.html
nodes.summary: Worker mobile wireframe (W8 Invoice photo), used in Unload and as a fallback in Wrong movement. A document camera with a page frame, torch and 'No invoice?' shortcut captures one or more invoice pages. A preview lets the worker retake, add a page or use the photos, and a progress card simulates Azure Document Intelligence reading the PO number, supplier and product lines. A successful read goes to W9 Review invoice (or back to W15 with the product found). An unreadable photo offers tips, a retake, or typing the details on W9. 'No invoice?' goes to W10, and Cancel returns to W3.
nodes.languageNotes: Simulates async AI document reading with chained 900 ms setTimeout ticks kept in a timers array, which is cleared on every state change so previews never overlap.

nodes.name: readingCard
nodes.summary: Renders the AI reading progress card (step checklist and progress bar). On failure it renders a 'Couldn't read the invoice' card with photo tips, a Retake button and a 'Type the details instead' fallback to W9.

nodes.name: setState
nodes.summary: Core state machine for the invoice camera. It manages multi-page capture (page badge, thumbnails, 'Use N pages') and the camera/preview views. It simulates the Azure Document Intelligence read with timed steps, then goes to W9 for Unload or back to W15 for Wrong movement.

nodes.name: W9-review-invoice.html
nodes.summary: Worker mobile wireframe (W9 Count and confirm), shown during Unload after the invoice is read. The ASN is matched by the PO number, or chosen from a list when none is found, and the AI-read invoice header (PO, supplier, invoice number and date) is shown. Each product line shows Expected (ASN), Invoice (AI-read, correctable) and Counted quantities, with instant 'short/more vs invoice/ASN' markers. Confirm is enabled only after every line is ticked as counted. Counted quantities become the Lot quantity. If counts differ, the screen goes to the W11 Summary and the differences go to the supervisor review queue; if all match, it returns to W3. Retake goes back to W8.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Renders the count-and-confirm form: the ASN match bar (or 'No ASN found' with Choose ASN), the AI-read invoice header, and per-product cards with Expected, Invoice and Counted numbers and variance markers. It keeps Confirm disabled until every line is counted, then goes to W11 when counts differ or to W3 when all match.

nodes.name: W10-no-invoice.html
nodes.summary: Worker mobile wireframe (W10 No invoice) for Unload deliveries that arrive without an invoice. The worker photographs the product, an AI step suggests an editable general product name (not linked to a catalogue), and the form requires only the counted quantity and unit. Optional supplier, PO number, invoice number and date, and product code fields are folded away. The worker can add several products. Confirm goes to W11 ASN match (automatic when a PO number is entered, otherwise chosen from a list), and Back returns to W8 Invoice photo.

nodes.name: setState
nodes.summary: Switches between the product camera, a simulated AI analysis (a 1.8 s timer that then opens the form), the blank AI-suggestion form, and a filled-in example with optional details.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Builds the no-invoice product form: the editable AI-suggested name, the required counted quantity and unit selector, collapsible optional invoice-style details, and 'Add another product'. Confirm stays disabled until quantity and unit are filled, then goes to W11 ASN match by PO number or to the ASN list.

nodes.name: W11-asn-match.html
nodes.summary: Worker mobile wireframe for the Unload activity's ASN check, shown after the invoice or product details are counted on W9/W10. It previews eight states: PO match, differences against the invoice and ASN (short, extra, missing, not on the ASN, unit differs), several ASNs for one PO, a partial second delivery that adds up, picking an open ASN from a searchable list filtered by supplier when there is no PO, matching an invoice-less product to an ASN line, and No ASN. The worker is never blocked: differences and No ASN go to the supervisor review queue, Fix quantities/Recount goes back to W9/W10, and Continue returns to W3 to shelve the goods.
nodes.languageNotes: Self-contained prototype: about half the file is inline Pulse CSS. Plain JS keeps a `state` variable; `buildStates` creates the preview buttons, `setState` resets the selection, and `render` rebuilds the screen's innerHTML from template literals. Screen navigation is only simulated with `toast()` messages such as 'Continue -> W3'.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: State-machine renderer for the ASN check. For each of the eight preview states (match, diff3, diff, multi, partial, choose, map, none) it builds the coloured result header, the expected/invoice/counted comparison rows, the shipment picker with supplier filter chips, or the ASN-line mapping dropdown, and wires Continue, Recount and Fix quantities to simulated navigation.

nodes.name: W12-pass-fail.html
nodes.summary: Worker wireframe for the Check activity. A product fetched from a shelf on W6 (e.g. Product X, LOT-1001, 20 boxes on Shelf R1) is marked Pass or Fail. Fail needs a reason chip or a description, takes an optional photo, and asks whether the product stays on the shelf or is moved; it then puts a Defective mark on just the fetched portion. Pass and Fail-move go to the W7 destination scan, Fail-stays returns to W3, and Change goes back to W6.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Renders the product card (Lot, quantity, shelf) and the Pass/Fail choice. On Fail it adds reason chips, a description field, the optional photo slot, the stay-or-move choice and the Defective-mark warning banner.

nodes.name: upd
nodes.summary: Pass/fail validation and routing for the confirm button. It stays disabled until a result is chosen; Pass routes to W7. Fail requires at least one reason chip or a non-empty description, then routes to W3 if the product stays or to W7 if it is moved.

nodes.name: W13-item-list.html
nodes.summary: Worker wireframe for building the item list of a Pack or Load activity, opened from '+ Add' on W3. It shows the item count and total quantity, then one row per product (source location, Lot, quantity, a DEFECTIVE tag when flagged) or packed unit, each with a remove button. + Add goes to W6 to scan a packing area or dock. Finish pack goes to W14 to create the Pack ID; Finish loading marks the units as loaded, removes them from stock and returns to W3.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Renders the Pack or Load item list: an empty-state hint, or totals per unit and item rows with source, Lot, defective tag and remove button. It also updates the Finish button label and routes it to W14 (pack) or W3 (load).

nodes.name: W14-pack-created.html
nodes.summary: Worker confirmation screen shown after 'Finish pack' on W13. It displays the system-generated, unique Pack ID (PACK-303) in large text, a reminder to write it on the package, and the contents grouped by invoice with product, Lot, source pack area and quantity; this is the permanent pack-to-lot traceability link. Scan dock goes to W7 to place the pack at a dock, and Edit/Back returns to W13 to fix the contents while keeping the Pack ID. The notes also raise an open question about printing Pack ID labels.

nodes.name: W15-wrong-movement.html
nodes.summary: Worker rework flow, started from Put away or Pick on W3, for reporting a product that someone put in the wrong place. A four-step wizard runs under a rework timer while the main activity is paused: find the product by shelf scan (W6) or invoice photo (W8), confirm it and the earlier movement (who, when, from where), give a required reason and optional photo that flags (never deletes) that movement, then scan the right location (W7). Rework time is saved separately from productivity, and Cancel or Back to Put away resumes the activity on W3.
nodes.languageNotes: Multi-step wizard driven by a single `state` string, with a `setInterval` rework timer that updates the header in place; reason validation is in a separate `upd` helper.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Drives the four-step wrong-movement wizard under a rework-timer header and stepper. The steps are: find (shelf scan or invoice photo, plus a 'shelf didn't match' fallback), confirm the product and the earlier movement by Employee 117, pick reasons to flag it, and move it to the suggested location. It ends with a Done summary showing the correction and the rework time.

nodes.name: W16-complete.html
nodes.summary: Worker summary screen shown after Stop is confirmed on W3, in the colour of whichever of the six activities was running (Unload, Check, Put away, Pick, Pack, Load). It shows the worker's time and quantity handled, every recorded move (lots created, check results, wrong-movement reports, packs created or loaded), time-based shares with co-workers (marked 'so far' while others are still working), and a plain 'Not recorded' warning for unfinished steps. 'Do another' opens the W2 start sheet and goes on to W3; Done returns to W2 Home.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Builds the completion summary for the selected activity and state (alone, shared, unfinished). It shows time and handled stats and the list of recorded moves; the shared state adds time-proportional share bars (60/40), and the unfinished state adds a Not-recorded warning. It also sets up the 'Do another' button.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Catalog page for the Pulse supervisor portal wireframes ('Pulse, for supervisors'), rendering linked cards grouped into Start (S1 Login, S2 Dashboard), Daily work (S7 Review queue, S8 Live stock, S9 Traceability) and Setup (S6 ASNs, S3 Employees, S4 Locations & labels, S5 Activity settings), each with a one-line purpose. It also links back to the worker app screen index and hosts the Daylight/Night shift theme switcher, defaulting to Daylight and persisted in localStorage.
nodes.languageNotes: The screen catalog is data-driven: a nested array (G) of group/screen tuples is mapped into card markup with template literals, so adding a screen is a one-line change.

nodes.name: S1-login.html
nodes.summary: Desktop supervisor login wireframe: a warehouse-photo panel with headline facts (items moved today, people on the floor, time vs target) beside an Employee ID + password form with show/hide toggle and a 'Forgot your password?' hint telling the user to ask another supervisor to reset it in Employees. A preview bar simulates Normal, Wrong password (tries remaining) and Locked states, warehouse workers are pointed to the phone app, and 'Log in' lands on the S2 dashboard.
nodes.languageNotes: The background photo is embedded as a base64 JPEG data URI and injected at runtime, keeping the prototype a single self-contained file.

nodes.name: S2-dashboard.html
nodes.summary: Supervisor dashboard wireframe and first screen after login: day picker, shift filter (All/Day/Night), Download Excel export (one sheet per view plus all activity records), five KPI tiles with sparklines (items moved, on the floor, time vs target, wrong movements, ASN match), an hourly items-moved chart stacked by activity, and a live 'On the floor now' list flagging activities near auto-close. Tabs present the five agreed views (By activity, By worker, Target comparison, Shared activities, Wrong movements & rework) with sortable columns, plus a review-queue summary linking to S7 and a weekly ASN status bar linking to S6.
nodes.languageNotes: All charts are hand-built SVG strings generated with template literals (no chart library); a window.onTheme hook redraws the hourly chart when the Daylight/Night theme changes so per-theme activity colours stay legible.

nodes.name: S3-employees.html
nodes.summary: Employees setup wireframe for managing who can log in: summary tiles (active workers, supervisors, working right now, locked accounts), filter chips (All, Workers, Supervisors, Locked, Inactive) with ID/name search, and a table of role, status, last activity and activities today. Supervisors can add an employee (unique numeric ID, optional name, Worker or Supervisor role) via a drawer that issues a one-time temporary password, reset passwords, unlock accounts locked after 5 wrong passwords, and deactivate or reactivate people (history is kept, and supervisors cannot deactivate themselves).

nodes.name: S4-locations.html
nodes.summary: Locations & labels setup wireframe listing every shelf, packing area and dock with code, name, type and current item count, filterable by type and searchable. Supervisors can add one location or a range of shelves (e.g. D1 to D12) through drawers, tick rows to batch-print barcode labels on A4 sheets, and see a live label preview (type, site BOM-3, large code, name, barcode, LOC- code). Notes state that codes are unique, occupied locations cannot be removed, and location type controls where Pick and Pack may end.
nodes.languageNotes: The barcode is decorative only: bars() seeds a linear congruential generator from a hash of the location code, so each code renders a stable, distinct-looking SVG bar pattern rather than real barcode symbology.

nodes.name: setS
nodes.summary: Switches the login preview between Normal, Wrong password and Locked states: highlights the active preview button, shows the matching error banner, hides Log in when the account is locked, and clears the password with a shake animation on a wrong attempt.

nodes.name: login
nodes.summary: Simulates a successful sign-in by replacing the Log in button with a spinner and redirecting to S2-dashboard.html after 700 ms.

nodes.name: drawHourly
nodes.summary: Renders the 'Items moved by hour' SVG stacked bar chart: computes a rounded axis maximum, draws grid lines and per-activity segments with a rounded top cap, marks the current hour, and wires hover hit-areas that show a per-activity breakdown tooltip.

nodes.name: drawFloor
nodes.summary: Renders the live 'On the floor now' list showing each running activity's employee, activity tag, current step and elapsed mm:ss timer, flagging ones near the auto-close limit; a one-second setInterval re-runs it to tick the timers.

nodes.name: drawView
nodes.summary: Renders the active tab of the five agreed reporting views: By activity (bar chart plus totals table), By worker (sortable table with productivity-vs-target bars and rework kept separate), Target comparison (average vs target with a status from statusOf), Shared activities (per-participant time-share split bars) and Wrong movements & rework.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Filters the employee list by the selected role/status chip and the ID or name search text, then renders rows with status pills, lock details and context-specific actions (Unlock, Reset password, Deactivate or Reactivate, none for the signed-in supervisor), or an empty state when nothing matches.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Resets an employee's password: generates a one-time temporary password, shows it in the modal, clears any account lock, and refreshes the summary tiles and table.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: Adds a new Active employee from the drawer form (ID, optional name defaulting to 'Employee <id>', selected role), refreshes the view, then shows the generated temporary password to hand over.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Filters locations by the type chip and code/name search, renders selectable rows with type badges, item counts (or Empty) and per-row Print buttons, then refreshes the label preview.

nodes.name: preview
nodes.summary: Updates the label preview panel for the current selection: a full label for the first selected location, a mini A4 sheet of up to nine labels with an overflow count, and a Print button whose caption and enabled state match the selection size.

nodes.name: addRange
nodes.summary: Bulk-creates shelf locations for an aisle letter and numeric range, skipping codes that already exist, selects the new shelves, refreshes the view, and reports how many labels were sent to the printer.

nodes.name: S5-activity-settings.html
nodes.summary: Supervisor setup screen (S5) for the six warehouse activities (Unload, Check, Put away, Pick, Pack, Load). Each activity card has steppers for the target time per activity and the auto-close limit, plus a "Today" bar showing the average time today against the target (on target / % faster / % slower). A save bar appears only when something changed (Discard or Save changes), saving is blocked unless auto-close is longer than the target, and a Change history panel records who changed what and when. Notes state that new values apply only to activities started after saving, and that auto-closed activities go to the review queue (S7).
nodes.languageNotes: Like every supervisor screen, it shares an inline JS shell that renders the Pulse side nav (S2-S9 plus a logout link to S1) and a persisted Night shift/Daylight theme switch. Domain data is hard-coded JS arrays/objects standing in for the real API.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Renders the six activity cards from the working copy: target and auto-close steppers, an Edited pill for changed cards, an inline error when auto-close is not longer than the target, and the today-vs-target bar with its status label. It also shows or hides the save bar with the count of unsaved activities and redraws the change history.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Save handler. It refuses to save if any auto-close limit is not longer than its target, adds a "Just now" history entry for every changed target or auto-close value, copies the edited values into the saved set, and confirms that new values apply to activities started from now.

nodes.name: S6-asns.html
nodes.summary: Supervisor setup screen (S6) for Advance Shipping Notices, i.e. what suppliers say is coming. A drop zone takes an Excel/CSV file filled in from the downloadable Pulse template (one row per product line); a bad file lists errors by row number and saves nothing. Summary tiles and status filter chips (Expected, Partly received, Received, Closed) sit over a searchable ASN table (ASN, PO number, supplier, expected date, lines, received-units progress, status). Clicking a row opens a drawer with expected vs received per line, the deliveries received against the ASN, the upload source (file, rows, uploader), and a Close ASN action that sends missing items to the review queue (S7). Matching to deliveries uses the PO number only.
nodes.languageNotes: Like every supervisor screen, it shares an inline JS shell that renders the Pulse side nav (S2-S9 plus a logout link to S1) and a persisted Night shift/Daylight theme switch. Domain data is hard-coded JS arrays/objects standing in for the real API.

nodes.name: upload
nodes.summary: Simulates an ASN file upload. The error path shows a banner listing row-level validation problems (empty PO number, non-numeric quantity, unit not in Boxes/Pallets/Pieces/Other) and saves nothing. The success path adds a new Expected ASN (ASN-2055 for PO-7822) to the list and refreshes the tiles and table.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: Opens the ASN detail drawer. It shows the status and received total, an expected vs received table per product line with a Match / Not yet / Missing / N to come / N extra result, the deliveries received against the ASN (Unload by an employee, with invoice or product photo), the upload source, and Close ASN only while the ASN is still open.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Filters the ASN list by the selected status chip and a free-text search over ASN, PO number and supplier, then renders table rows with a received-percentage progress bar and a status pill (empty state when nothing matches).

nodes.name: S7-review-queue.html
nodes.summary: Supervisor daily-work screen (S7) collecting everything that needs a supervisor decision, in four tabbed queues with counts: Auto-closed activities, ASN differences, Wrong movements and Defective products. It uses a list on the left and details on the right. For an auto-closed activity the supervisor sees the start / last scan / auto-close timeline and confirms or corrects the end time, which updates that worker's productivity. ASN differences show expected vs received (short, extra, missing, not on ASN, unit differs) with a note and Mark reviewed, linking to S6. Wrong movements show the original move, who found it, the reason and the rework time, with Acknowledge and links to the Lot history in S9. Defective items show the reason and photo, and the supervisor either clears the Defective mark after re-checking or keeps it. Every decision is saved with the supervisor ID and time, and resolved items slide out of the list.
nodes.languageNotes: Like every supervisor screen, it shares an inline JS shell that renders the Pulse side nav (S2-S9 plus a logout link to S1) and a persisted Night shift/Daylight theme switch. Domain data is hard-coded JS arrays/objects standing in for the real API. The side-nav badge is updated live with the remaining item count.

nodes.name: detail
nodes.summary: Builds the right-hand detail panel for the selected item based on the active queue. Auto-closed: activity timeline plus an editable corrected end time (default is the last scan) with Save corrected time / Keep. ASN difference: expected-vs-received table, note field, Mark reviewed and an Open ASN link to S6. Wrong movement: move/report/correction timeline, rework time, Lot link and See full history (S9) with Acknowledge. Defective: photo, location, reason, a worker-warning banner, and Re-checked clear mark / Keep as Defective.

nodes.name: resolve
nodes.summary: Applies a supervisor decision to the selected item. It animates the row out, removes it from its queue, selects the next (or previous) item, re-renders tabs, list and detail, and shows a confirmation toast such as "End time set to ... Productivity updated." or "Defective mark cleared".

nodes.name: tabs
nodes.summary: Renders the four queue tabs with their icons and item counts, updates the header to "N items need a decision", and keeps the side-nav review-queue badge in sync with the total open items.

nodes.name: S8-live-stock.html
nodes.summary: Supervisor daily-work screen (S8) showing what the system believes is on every location right now. Summary tiles count locations in use, Lots and packs in stock, locations with defective items, and packed units waiting at docks. A clickable warehouse map shows storage shelves by aisle (A-C, 1-6) plus receiving shelf R1, pack areas and docks, each with a fill bar, a defective flag, or an empty style. Selecting a location lists each Lot portion or packed unit on it (product, Lot, quantity and unit, invoice, who placed it and when) with a "Trace history" link to S9. Search by product, Lot or invoice dims every location that does not hold it, and Export downloads the stock list to Excel. Part-moves appear as portions of the same Lot, and floor differences are fixed by workers through Wrong movement.
nodes.languageNotes: Like every supervisor screen, it shares an inline JS shell that renders the Pulse side nav (S2-S9 plus a logout link to S1) and a persisted Night shift/Daylight theme switch. Domain data is hard-coded JS arrays/objects standing in for the real API.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Renders the aisle grid and the receiving/packing/dock areas, then fills the side panel for the selected location. Each Lot or packed-unit entry shows product, defective count, Lot and invoice, who placed it and when, quantity with unit, and a Trace history link to S9 (or an empty state).

nodes.name: find
nodes.summary: Search handler. It finds every location whose stock matches the query by product, Lot or invoice, dims the rest of the map, moves the selection to the first match if the current location is not one, and redraws.

nodes.name: cell
nodes.summary: Builds one location tile for the map: code, product or "N lots" caption, a defective "!" flag, a fill bar scaled to the location capacity, and the selected/empty/dimmed states.

nodes.name: S9-traceability.html
nodes.summary: Supervisor investigation screen (S9) that follows any Lot, packed unit, invoice or PO "from the truck to the truck" from one search box, with quick examples (LOT-1001, PACK-301, INV-55, PO-7781, LOT-0987). A Lot shows its header (invoice, PO, supplier, ASN match, total received and accounted for), where every portion is now with a split bar, a split tree of portions, and a timeline of every move (who, when, from where to where). A packed unit shows its contents (product, Lot, invoice, source, quantity) and its journey to the dock and truck. An invoice or PO lists all Lots received with it, where they are now and the ASN match. Wrong movements stay in the history, flagged, with the correction linked, and portions always add up to the Lot's original quantity. The notes cite Developer Feature Guide sections 8.4 and 3.3.
nodes.languageNotes: Like every supervisor screen, it shares an inline JS shell that renders the Pulse side nav (S2-S9 plus a logout link to S1) and a persisted Night shift/Daylight theme switch. Domain data is hard-coded JS arrays/objects standing in for the real API. Results are pre-baked HTML templates chosen by a lookup on the normalised query.

nodes.name: go
nodes.summary: Trace dispatcher. It normalises the search text (upper case, no spaces) and maps it to the matching result builder: Lot (LOT-1001, LOT-0987), packed unit (PACK-301), or invoice/PO (INV-55, PO-7781 or 7781). Unknown IDs get a "Nothing found" panel that explains the ID formats.

nodes.name: lot1001
nodes.summary: Builds the full Lot trace for LOT-1001: header with invoice/PO/supplier and ASN match, a where-is-it-now strip and proportional split bar (Shelf B1, Shelf A4, Pack Area 1), a split tree of portions with the employees involved, and a chronological movement timeline from Unload through Check, a part-move, a shared Put away and Pick.

nodes.name: lot0987
nodes.summary: Builds the Lot trace for LOT-0987, the wrong-movement example. The timeline keeps the wrong Put away flagged in the history and follows it with the report (reason, found by shelf scan) and the linked correction move, with rework time kept separate.

layers.name: Specifications & Planning
layers.description: Pulse POC specification deliverables: the Developer Feature Guide, the Data Model and Build Plan PDFs, and the Build Tasks workbook that sequences 9 sprints and 38 PRs against screens and tables.

layers.name: Worker Mobile App Wireframes
layers.description: Clickable phone wireframes W1-W16 for warehouse workers (login, activity timer, sharing/joining, scanning, unload with invoice/ASN matching, pass/fail checks, packing, wrong movements), plus the worker screen hub and the Pulse showcase page.

layers.name: Supervisor Web Portal Wireframes
layers.description: Desktop wireframes S1-S9 for supervisors (login, productivity dashboard, employee/location/activity-setting setup, ASN upload, review queue, live stock and lot traceability) and their catalog hub page.

layers.name: Database Foundation & Master Data
layers.description: The PostgreSQL DDL file for the pt schema together with the site-scoped master and setup tables (site, employee, location, activity type, activity settings and their change history) that nearly every other table references.

layers.name: Activity Tracking & Productivity Reporting
layers.description: Timed work records (activity, participant, raw tap/scan event_log) and the chained productivity views that roll them into participant time, activity quantity, time shares and per-worker daily totals.

layers.name: Receiving & ASN Data
layers.description: Inbound flow tables from supervisor ASN uploads (asn_upload, asn, asn_line) through worker receipts and receipt lines, plus the view that compares received against expected ASN quantities.

layers.name: Stock & Traceability Data
layers.description: Lots, packs, portions and movements that track where received goods sit and how they move between locations, with the stock-on-location and lot-balance views behind live stock and traceability screens.

layers.name: Quality & Review Data
layers.description: Quality and exception records (check results, defect marks, wrong movements, blob-stored photos) and the supervisor review_item queue that points to exactly one flagged subject row.

tour.title: Pulse at a Glance
tour.description: Pulse is a productivity-tracking proof of concept for warehouse operations, prepared for Kuehne + Nagel. There is no README, so the Developer Feature Guide (v1.7) serves as the project overview: it describes one web app with a single Employee-ID login, where the role decides between phone screens for workers (W1-W16) and desktop screens for supervisors (S1-S9). Everything is built around six warehouse activities: Unload, Check, Put away, Pick, Pack and Load. Keep Wireframes/index.html open as your map for the tour; it groups all 16 worker screens by stage and links to the Showcase and the supervisor portal.

tour.title: Build Plan and Sprints
tour.description: The Build Plan (v1.2) sets the stack: a Python 3.12 FastAPI backend with SQLAlchemy 2 and Alembic on Azure Database for PostgreSQL, one React + TypeScript + Vite PWA that shows worker or supervisor screens depending on the user's role, and Azure Blob Storage, Document Intelligence and AI Vision. It also sets the architecture (REST plus WebSocket live updates, APScheduler jobs for auto-close, retention and invoice reading, with business rules kept in backend services) and splits the work into 38 single-feature PRs across Sprints 0-8, from Foundations to Hardening. The Build Tasks workbook tracks the same PRs in dependency order. Each row names the wireframe screens and database tables the PR touches, so it is the best index for linking the screens and tables in the rest of this tour.

tour.title: Data Model Foundations
tour.description: The Data Model PDF explains in plain prose the PostgreSQL schema that the Database Schema SQL file creates: 23 UUID-keyed tables in the pt schema, plus an audit trigger, indexes and 8 reporting views. Its main design decisions apply to every table you will meet later: UUID keys with separate human-readable codes (LOT-, PACK-, PA-), a site_id on almost every table, IST timestamptz values, whole-number quantities, and no deletes except purging old photos and event-log rows. Three tables form the foundation: site is the root tenant that every business row points to, employee holds workers and supervisors with their numeric employee_code, role and lockout fields, and location holds the scannable shelves, packing areas and docks, each with a code unique within its site.
tour.languageLesson: SQL constraints as business rules: the schema enforces its rules inside the database. A CHECK limits employee.role to worker or supervisor, a composite UNIQUE (site_id, location_code) makes codes unique only within a site, and foreign keys tie rows to site. Every API path, Alembic migration and ad-hoc script must then follow the same rules.

tour.title: Worker Login and Home
tour.description: The worker journey starts at W1, where a numeric Employee ID and password open a shift; errors never say which field was wrong, and the account locks after 5 wrong passwords. W1 writes to employee for the lockout counters and to event_log, the raw log of every tap and scan with both device_time and server_time. W2 Home then shows the worker's 'My day' rings and six colour-coded activity tiles from the fixed activity_type lookup, where each type also names the location type a move must end on. Starting a tile opens W3 (or W8 Invoice photo for Unload), and only one activity can run at a time.

tour.title: Running, Sharing and Joining
tour.description: W3 is the single running-activity screen for all six activities, with a live timer, the people working, the activity's steps and one large button for the next scan. Behind it, an activity row is one unit of work with a human code such as PA-5095, and it copies the target and auto-close minutes when it starts, so later settings changes never apply to past work. Each worker on the activity gets a participant row with their own joined_at and stopped_at, so sharing on W4 (QR code plus activity code) and joining on W5 simply add another participant. The partial unique index participant_one_running ensures a worker never has more than one open activity.
tour.languageLesson: PostgreSQL partial unique index: a UNIQUE index with a WHERE clause enforces uniqueness only on rows that match the condition. Here participant_one_running covers only open participations, so a worker can have many finished participations but never two running ones. The rule holds even when two requests arrive at the same moment.

tour.title: Scanning and Moving Stock
tour.description: Most activities reuse the same scan pair launched from W3: W6 scans a source location (or the worker types the code) and shows what is there, including a Defective warning and a quantity stepper, and W7 scans the destination, rejecting a wrong location type, the source itself or an unknown barcode. Each confirmed move adds a row to movement, a never-edited ledger with types such as unload_place, put_away, pick, pack_add, load and correction, whose from and to locations must differ. A partial move splits a portion, a piece of a Lot in one place that links to its parent through parent_portion_id. Live portions therefore always add up to the Lot's received quantity.

tour.title: Unload: Invoice and Count
tour.description: Unload records the most data of any activity: W8 photographs one or more invoice pages for Azure Document Intelligence to read, and W10 handles deliveries with no invoice by photographing the product and suggesting a product name with AI. W9 then shows each product line with Expected (ASN), Invoice (AI-read and correctable) and Counted quantities, and Confirm only unlocks when every line is ticked as counted. These screens write a receipt (one per delivery, with the invoice header and the raw AI result in ai_raw jsonb) and receipt_line rows comparing expected, invoice and counted quantities. Each counted line becomes the quantity of a new Lot.
tour.languageLesson: PostgreSQL jsonb: receipt.ai_raw keeps the full, semi-structured Document Intelligence response alongside the normalised columns the app actually queries, such as invoice number, PO and supplier. You can inspect or re-parse the original AI read later without changing the schema.

tour.title: Matching Against the ASN
tour.description: After counting, W11 compares the delivery with the supplier's Advance Shipping Notice, previewing states such as a PO match, short, extra or missing lines, not on the ASN, unit differs, partial second deliveries, choosing an ASN from a list, and No ASN. The worker is never blocked, because differences go to the supervisor review queue. Matching uses asn.po_number_norm, a STORED generated column that upper-cases the PO number and strips spaces and the PO prefix, backed by a partial index over open ASNs. asn_line holds the expected product lines, and the v_asn_line_received view sums counted quantities across deliveries so an ASN can move from expected to partly_received, received or closed.
tour.languageLesson: Generated columns: GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED makes PostgreSQL compute a value such as po_number_norm on every insert or update. The normalisation rule lives in one place and the result can be indexed. receipt has its own generated po_number_norm, so both sides of the match are normalised the same way.

tour.title: Check, Pack and Load
tour.description: During Check, a product fetched on W6 is marked Pass or Fail on W12; a Fail needs a reason chip or a description, can include a photo, and places a Defective mark on that portion only, while check_result stores the quantity, pass/fail, reason_codes text[] and whether the product stayed on the location. Pack and Load reuse the scan pattern from Step 6 to build an item list on W13. Finish pack creates a packed unit, and W14 shows its system-generated Pack ID (for example PACK-303) for the worker to write on the package. The pack table records that unit, the Pack activity that created it, an optional dock location and its status (open, at_dock, loaded), with CHECKs that require a location at the dock and a loaded_at time once loaded.

tour.title: Finishing and Productivity Math
tour.description: Sliding to stop on W3 opens W16, which summarises the worker's time, the quantity handled, every recorded move, and time-based shares with co-workers. These numbers are calculated by views, not stored. v_participant_time works out each worker's minutes (using a supervisor-corrected stop time where there is one, minus rework), v_activity_quantity sums movement quantities without correction moves, and v_participant_share builds on them with window functions to produce share_fraction, share_qty and job_productivity_pct (target / job minutes x 100). This is the shared-activity rule written in SQL: quantity is split by time worked, and job productivity is credited to each worker in proportion to their share.
tour.languageLesson: SQL window functions: an expression such as SUM(minutes) OVER (PARTITION BY activity_id) puts the per-activity total on every participant row, unlike GROUP BY, which collapses rows. That is how a view can compute each worker's fraction of a shared job in a single query.

tour.title: Supervisor Portal and Dashboard
tour.description: The supervisor portal hub groups the desktop screens into Start, Daily work and Setup. S1 is the desktop login, using the same Employee ID and password and showing a Locked state like W1. S2 Dashboard is the first screen after login: KPI tiles, an hourly chart of items moved, a live 'On the floor now' list that flags activities close to auto-close, and the five agreed views (By activity, By worker, Target comparison, Shared activities, Wrong movements & rework) with Excel export. Its figures come from the views in Step 10 plus v_activity_time (job minutes from the first join to the last stop) and v_worker_day (totals per worker per IST day, with a share-weighted productivity_pct).

tour.title: Supervisor Setup Screens
tour.description: The Setup screens manage the master data the worker app relies on: S3 Employees adds workers and supervisors with a one-time temporary password, resets passwords and unlocks locked accounts, and S4 Locations & labels creates single locations or shelf ranges and batch-prints barcode labels. S6 ASNs uploads Excel/CSV files based on the Pulse template, rejects a bad file with its errors listed by row, and offers Close ASN. S5 Activity settings edits the per-site target and auto-close minutes in activity_setting, where a CHECK requires auto-close to be longer than the target and a trigger writes every change to setting_change. Because activities copy these values when they start (Step 5), a new setting never changes past results.
tour.languageLesson: Audit triggers: the BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger trg_activity_setting_history saves old and new values in the same transaction as the change itself. No code path that writes activity_setting can skip the history in setting_change.

tour.title: Live Stock and Traceability
tour.description: This step brings the stock model together: a lot is one received batch created from exactly one receipt line (Step 7), with an auto-generated code such as LOT-1001, while portions record where its pieces are now and the movement ledger records how they got there. S8 Live stock reads v_stock_on_location to draw a warehouse map with quantities and defective flags per location. S9 Traceability follows any Lot, packed unit, invoice or PO 'from the truck to the truck', with a split tree and a full timeline of moves. The v_lot_balance view is a control check that compares each Lot's received_qty with the sum of its portions, confirming the portion-split rule still holds.

tour.title: Quality and Review Loop
tour.description: The last loop connects workers and supervisors without ever blocking work on the floor. During Put away or Pick, a worker reports an earlier misplaced product on W15, which creates a wrong_movement row linking the original movement (flagged, never deleted) to a new correction movement, with rework time kept out of productivity; failed checks from Step 9 leave a defect_mark that only a supervisor can clear. These cases, along with auto-closed activities and ASN differences, become review_item rows, each pointing to exactly one subject row. In S7 Review queue, supervisors correct auto-close end times, mark ASN differences reviewed, acknowledge wrong moves, and clear or keep Defective marks, and every decision is saved with the supervisor's ID and the time.
tour.languageLesson: Polymorphic references with num_nonnulls: a CHECK such as num_nonnulls(col_a, col_b, col_c) = 1 requires exactly one of several nullable foreign keys to be set. review_item and photo use this to point at one kind of subject while keeping real, enforced foreign keys.
